covers: Tuesday 27 October 2026 from 21:15 to 22:15 SAST: late Wall Street trade, Visa's results after the close and Israel's exit polls, ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision
headline: Nasdaq up about 1.4% late in the day on chips; Visa beats with 13% revenue growth and a 16% dividend rise; Israel's exit polls show no clear winner
summary: The rand was steady at R16.65/$ on Tuesday with the 2035 bond yield at 8.62% (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct). At 3:44 p.m. New York time, minutes before the close, the S&P 500 was up 0.74% at 7,733.55, the Nasdaq up 1.38% at 26,530.47 and the Dow up 0.14% at 52,432.37 (Yahoo Finance, 27 Oct), and after the close Visa reported 13% revenue growth to $12.1 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.48 (Visa results via Stock Titan, 27 Oct). Brent fell $2.09 to $113.72 and WTI $1.93 to $99.83 at 17:44 GMT as Middle East talks continued (Reuters via GV Wire, 27 Oct), while Israel's TV exit polls showed neither Netanyahu's coalition nor the main opposition alliance with a clear majority (Al Jazeera, 27 Oct).

items.title: Houthis say a missile hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery; Riyadh has not confirmed
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they hit Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery with 550,000 barrels a day of capacity, with a ballistic missile, causing a fire at the complex, which includes a shipping terminal. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike; Bloomberg reported a fire near the terminal had been contained. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh, and an air raid alert was briefly issued in the capital on Tuesday afternoon (Reuters via Investing.com, 27 Oct). Damage and any effect on exports are still unclear.

items.title: Ras Tanura fire contained; Saudi Arabia says it intercepted Houthi missiles
items.summary: A fire near Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's biggest oil export hub, was quickly contained after an attack early on Tuesday. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Region and four drones aimed at the south. The extent of damage, and whether exports were affected, is still unclear; the Shaybah field is reported unaffected (Oilprice.com, citing Bloomberg, 27 Oct).

items.title: US consumer confidence jumps to 91.7, well above forecasts
items.summary: The Conference Board's index rose to 91.7 in October from 84.2 in September (slightly revised up). The present situation index rose 8.6 points to 120.4 and expectations rose 6.9 points to 72.6 (The Conference Board, 27 Oct). Economists had expected about 81.2, so this is a 10.5-point beat, although plans to buy big-ticket goods and travel weakened and 12-month inflation expectations were still high at 5.8% (ActionForex, 27 Oct). A stronger consumer adds to the case the Fed weighs on Wednesday.

items.title: Israel exit polls: no clear winner as neither bloc reaches a majority
items.summary: After voting closed at 10pm local time on Tuesday 27 October, TV exit polls projected no outright winner: neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor the main opposition alliance appears to have a clear majority in the 120-seat Knesset, where 61 seats are needed (Al Jazeera, 27 Oct). Turnout was high; by 2pm it had reached 44.9%, the highest on record for that hour, and the shekel gained 1.2% against the dollar during the day (Times of Israel, 27 Oct). Why it matters: a long coalition fight could keep uncertainty over Israel's role in the wider Gulf conflict, which is holding oil near $100 a barrel or more.

items.title: Wall Street ends higher; Nasdaq up about 1.4% late in the day as chip stocks gain again
items.summary: At 3:44 p.m. New York time (21:44 SAST), shortly before the close, the S&P 500 was up 56.78 points, or 0.74%, at 7,733.55, the Nasdaq up 361.09 points, or 1.38%, at 26,530.47 and the Dow up 0.14% at 52,432.37; the 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.99% (Yahoo Finance, 27 Oct). Earlier, at 11:52 a.m., chip stocks were up 3.2% for a third straight gain and Broadcom almost 4% (AP via The Spokesman-Review, 27 Oct). Among the biggest S&P 500 fallers at 12:37 p.m. were Xylem (-11.9%), Boeing (-9.7%) and Valero (-7.8%) (TheStreet, 27 Oct). Official closing levels were not yet published at the time of writing.
items.source: Yahoo Finance; AP via The Spokesman-Review; TheStreet

items.title: GM up about 6% after saying it will move its listing to Nasdaq
items.summary: General Motors shares were up 6.3% at 11:52 a.m. New York time after the carmaker said it would switch its stock listing to Nasdaq (AP via The Spokesman-Review, 27 Oct); they had been up nearly 5% at 10:00am. Earlier, SoFi was up 11.4% before the open after results, while UPS rose 1.6% after beating forecasts and raising full-year guidance (TheStreet, 27 Oct).

items.title: Boeing falls about 9.5% after a wider loss and a later 737 target
items.summary: Boeing was down 9.5% at 11:52 a.m. New York time after CEO Kelly Ortberg said the company would not reach its 737 production-rate target "until early 2027" (AP via The Spokesman-Review, 27 Oct). Its adjusted third-quarter loss was $0.34 a share against the $0.20 analysts expected; the commercial airplanes unit's operating margin worsened to minus 6.5% and its revenue fell 3% to $10.72 billion, although free cash flow was a positive $464 million (24/7 Wall St., 27 Oct). Boeing delivered 161 commercial jets in the quarter and kept its full-year guidance (MoneyCheck, 27 Oct).
items.source: AP via The Spokesman-Review; 24/7 Wall St.; MoneyCheck

items.title: UPS beats and raises its 2026 outlook again
items.summary: UPS third-quarter revenue rose 6.7% to $22.9 billion, with adjusted earnings of $1.69 a share ($1.37 on a GAAP basis) and an adjusted operating margin of 9.0%. It now expects 2026 revenue of about $92.6 billion, adjusted earnings of about $7.28 a share and adjusted free cash flow of about $6.1 billion (IndexBox, citing the UPS release, 27 Oct).

items.title: PayPal beats on profit, misses on revenue, raises its 2026 forecast
items.summary: PayPal's third-quarter adjusted EPS was $1.45 against a $1.31 consensus, but revenue of $8.58 billion, up 2%, was below the $8.71 billion expected. It raised its 2026 adjusted EPS forecast to $5.60 from $5.38 and guided to $1.43 for the fourth quarter, above the $1.35 consensus. The shares were 0.3% lower at 7:15 a.m. New York time (13:15 SAST) (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: HSBC slides after results; FTSE 100 down 0.9% in early trade
items.summary: HSBC's third-quarter pre-tax profit rose 32% to $9.6 billion, in line with the bank's compiled forecasts, and it announced another buyback of up to $1 billion, but wealth revenue was flat at $2.7 billion after 15% and 23% growth in the first two quarters; the shares fell 5% in Hong Kong (Reuters via The Star, 27 Oct). In London the FTSE 100 fell 94 points, or 0.9%, to 10,673 in early Tuesday trade from Monday's close of 10,767.33, and the FTSE 250 was down 46 points at 24,455 (Share Talk, 27 Oct, 09:19 UTC).

items.title: Fed meeting starts; markets price an 82% chance of a December hike
items.summary: Traders price about an 11% chance of a Fed rate hike at this week's meeting and an 82% chance of an increase in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct). The decision is on Wednesday at 20:00 SAST. On Monday the S&P 500 closed at 7,676.77, the Nasdaq at 26,169.38 and the Dow at 52,361.58 (Reuters via Business Recorder, 26 Oct close).

items.title: Asia: Nikkei up 2.2% and KOSPI up 3.6% at midday on the chip rally
items.summary: At midday on Tuesday the Nikkei 225 was up 2.2% at 63,542.77 and the KOSPI up 3.6% at 5,667.99, while the Hang Seng slipped 0.2% to 23,174.44 and the Shanghai Composite 0.1% to 3,692.58 (AP via WSB Radio, 27 Oct).

items.title: Results tomorrow: Microsoft and Alphabet after Wednesday's close
items.summary: Visa reported after Tuesday's close (see Our coverage). Microsoft and Alphabet report on Wednesday 28 October and Amazon on Thursday (Nasdaq earnings calendar, 27 Oct).

items.title: SA leading indicator rises 1.1% in August; rand steady near R16.65/$
items.summary: The SARB's leading business cycle indicator rose 1.1% month on month in August after a 0.8% fall in July (Newsquawk, 27 Oct). The index tracks items such as vehicle sales, business confidence and money supply; one month's rise can be revised or reversed. Before the release the rand was at 16.6525 to the dollar, little changed, and the 2035 government bond yield was 8.62% (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct).

items.title: Moody's seen as most likely to upgrade South Africa, possibly within a year
items.summary: After Moody's called the medium-term budget 'credit positive', Business Day reports an upgrade from Ba2 (positive outlook since May) could come within about a year. Bank of America sees Moody's as the most likely agency to act, possibly to Ba1, and calls an S&P move to BB+ 'a closer call'; Investec's Annabel Bishop expects a Moody's upgrade in about 18 months, and Treasury says Moody's and S&P could upgrade within 12 to 18 months. Moody's and S&P review South Africa on 27 November and Fitch on 11 December. Moody's says a track record of fiscal delivery still has to be built (Business Day, 27 Oct). No rating action has been announced.

items.title: JSE shrugs off Brazil's crash; rand near R16.64/$
items.summary: The JSE All Share closed at 109,130.32 on Monday, up about 1.0% from Friday's 108,020.10, and the Top 40 at 100,977.01, up about 1.0% (Yahoo Finance via LRC Market Dashboard, 26 Oct). Brazil's Ibovespa closed down 13.88% at 176,608 and the dollar rose about 8.4% to near R$5.41 after Lula's re-election (Rio Times, 26 Oct). The rand was at 16.6371 to the dollar early on Tuesday, against 16.6125 on Monday morning (Yahoo Finance, 27 Oct; Reuters via Channel Africa, 26 Oct).
items.source: Rio Times; Channel Africa (Reuters); Yahoo Finance

items.title: Brent falls about $2 to $113.72 as Middle East talks continue; gold near $4,027
items.summary: Brent was down $2.09, or 1.8%, at $113.72 a barrel and WTI down $1.93, or 1.9%, at $99.83 at 17:44 GMT (19:44 SAST). Iranian state media said Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan agreed to continue talks on peace and security, although the Houthis said they struck Ras Tanura; UBS now expects Brent near $110 to year-end, up from $100 (Reuters via GV Wire, 27 Oct). Brent touched $117 on Monday, its highest since April. Gold futures were down 0.29% at $4,026.60 at 8:08am New York time (14:08 SAST) (TheStreet, 27 Oct).

items.title: Aramco offers Europe extra spot oil after restarting the East-West pipeline
items.summary: Saudi Aramco offered late-October spot cargoes to Europe at a discount to its official price, loading from Yanbu on the Red Sea or Sidi Kerir in Egypt, then offered more November cargoes and told European refiners they will get their full contracted November volumes, reversing October cancellations, now that the East-West pipeline shut by an attack is running again (Oilprice.com, citing Bloomberg, 27 Oct). Saudi Arabia normally ships 700,000 to 800,000 barrels a day to Europe.

items.title: OPEC+ expected to keep December quotas unchanged on Sunday
items.summary: The seven OPEC+ members that have been raising output (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman) are expected to leave quotas unchanged for December at Sunday's meeting, according to sources cited by Reuters. They finished unwinding 1.65 million barrels a day of 2023 cuts in September, and attention is turning to 2027 production baselines (Oilprice.com, 27 Oct). No decision has been announced yet.

items.title: Dollar firm; yen weaker before Bank of Japan decision
items.summary: The dollar index was at 102.05 (+0.09%), the yen at 157.73 per dollar, EUR/USD at 1.1172 and GBP/USD at 1.3342 on Tuesday morning in Asia. The Bank of Japan is expected to hold at 1.25% on Friday (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: KO: Coca-Cola beats and raises its outlook, but shares slip before the open
items.summary: For the quarter to 2 October, Coca-Cola's net revenue rose 7% to $13.4 billion, organic revenue rose 7%, unit case volume rose 5%, and comparable EPS rose 11% to $0.91. It raised its 2026 guidance to at least 5% organic revenue growth (from about 5%) and at least 11% comparable EPS growth (from 9% to 10%) (Coca-Cola results release, 27 Oct); Quartz reports both earnings and revenue beat expectations (Quartz, 27 Oct). KO closed at $92.70 on Monday and is a HOLD on the LRC Stock Scanner, held back by an LRC Analyst Target below the price (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Oct close). Even so, the shares were 1.61% lower at $91.22 before the bell at 8:49am New York time (TheStreet, 27 Oct). The higher guidance may lift estimates, but the rating is unchanged.

items.title: V: Visa beats, grows revenue 13% and raises its dividend 16%
items.summary: For the quarter to September, Visa's net revenue rose 13% to $12.1 billion, adjusted EPS rose 17% to $3.48 (GAAP $3.19) and payments volume grew 9% in constant dollars; for the full year revenue rose 15% to $45.9 billion. It returned $5.2 billion through buybacks and dividends in the quarter and raised its quarterly dividend 16% to $0.78 (Visa results release via Stock Titan, 27 Oct, released 4:05 p.m. New York time). Analysts had expected EPS of $3.44 (Alphastreet, 27 Oct), so profit came in slightly ahead. V closed at $404.20 on Monday and is a HOLD on the LRC Stock Scanner, held back by an LRC Analyst Target below the price (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Oct close); rating unchanged. Alphabet (GOOGL, a BUY) reports on Wednesday.

items.title: MSFT: Microsoft offers buyouts to about 60,000 staff a day before results
items.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees at vice-president level and below on selected teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK, with some data-centre, sales and marketing staff excluded; the package is 'similar to a standard severance offer' and the company expects fewer takers than for a July retirement-age offer (Bloomberg via Investing.com, 26 Oct). That is roughly a quarter of the 223,000 staff it had at the end of June. Microsoft closed at $532.60 on Monday, up 1.5% (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Oct close), and reports results on Wednesday 28 October. MSFT is a HOLD on the LRC Stock Scanner, held back by the LRC Analyst Target of $513.80 (about 4% below the price); rating unchanged.

items.title: META, NVDA and AMD: Nvidia and AMD put $4 billion into Meta's share sale
items.summary: Nvidia is buying $3 billion and AMD $1 billion of Meta's $25 billion common stock sale, priced at $625 a share, part of a nearly $98 billion equity funding plan; orders came to about five times the shares on offer (TipRanks, 27 Oct). On Tuesday Meta fell as much as 1.4% to $621.47, AMD rose 3% and Nvidia was flat (TipRanks, 27 Oct). The offerings are expected to close on 29 October (TokenPost, 27 Oct). By 11:52 a.m. New York time Meta was down 0.8% after raising its largest-ever equity fundraising to $97.5 billion (AP via The Spokesman-Review, 27 Oct). META, NVDA and AMD are on the LRC Stock Scanner; ratings unchanged.
items.source: TipRanks; TokenPost; AP via The Spokesman-Review

items.title: NVIDIA: Asian chip rally follows Monday's 2.4% gain
items.summary: NVIDIA closed up 2.39% at $216.00 on Monday (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct), and chip stocks extended gains in Asia on Tuesday, with the KOSPI up more than 4% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 27 Oct). Results are due on 17 November. NVDA is a BUY on the LRC Stock Scanner; rating unchanged.
